page: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 260 MB of L3 cache alongside specialized instruction extensions including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The hardware allocation pairs these computational cores with 256 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for resource-dense setups.

Local ephemeral storage is provided via a bundled 1890 GB NVMe solid-state drive, enabling low-latency temporary caching, scratchpad computations, or high-throughput paging operations. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong performance in uncached large-block read operations with 208.86 GB/sec memory bandwidth, Geekbench scores reaching 2,061 single-core and 17,016 multi-core, and static web serving throughput of 54.13 GB/sec. CPU-driven inference benchmarks reflect top-tier results for small language models, registering 373.84 tokens per second during text generation.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of a generous memory footprint, local NVMe capacity, and AMX acceleration makes the E32ds_v6 cost-effective for memory-constrained workloads without requiring dedicated accelerator hardware. The server is well suited for hosting in-memory database layers, Redis clusters, large relational databases, big data analytics engines, and CPU-based vector indexing.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, backed by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with 16 physical cores and 260 MB of L3 cache, the system supports modern vector and matrix instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. It includes 1890 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage for low-latency temporary data requirements. Benchmark testing highlights strong memory read bandwidth at 208.86 GB/sec and capable single-core and multi-core computational throughput, alongside competitive CPU-based machine learning inference. With its 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and rapid local scratch storage, the E32ds_v6 is tailored for memory-intensive enterprise workloads such as in-memory caches, large-scale relational database engines, high-throughput static web serving, and analytical data processing pipelines.
